quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Is not safe for motorcycles at any time.
Is usually safe for motorcycles, unless it is raining.
Should always be avoided because other parts of the lane do not have oil.
Adds traction for most motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually safe for motorcycles, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip down the center of the lane. When the road is dry, this area gives motorcycles enough traction to ride safely. The strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can ride beside it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front and rear brakes provide equal stopping power.
The front brake provides more stopping power than the rear brake.
The rear brake provides more stopping power than the front brake.
Only use the front brake when stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake provides more stopping power than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the total stopping power. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: The center of a lane:

options.text: Is always the best part of the lane for a motorcycle.
Often has oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
Often has oil and grease, and is never safe for riding.
Is the smoothest part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often has oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip down the center of each lane. When the road is dry, this area still gives motorcycles enough traction to ride safely. Avoid riding on large buildup of oil and grease, which is often found at busy intersections or near toll booths.

questions.question: When going through a curve, you should:

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane throughout the curve.
Always stay in the left part of the lane throughout the curve.
Always stay in the right part of the lane throughout the curve.
Remember that the best path may not follow the curve of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remember that the best path may not follow the curve of the road.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions can change at any time. Be ready to change your lane position when needed. The best path through a curve does not always follow the curve of the road.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you from behind, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay in the right part of the lane.
Move onto the shoulder.
Turn on your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When another vehicle passes you from behind or from the front, stay in the center of your lane. Riding closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: As your weight moves forward while braking, you:

options.text: Can apply the front brake harder.
Should use less pressure on the front brake.
Can apply the rear brake harder.
Lose traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can apply the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: When you brake, your weight shifts forward. This increases the traction available to the front wheel. This means you can apply the front brake with more force.

questions.question: When using the front brake, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
Grab the brake with only two fingers.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.
Stomp hard on the brake lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
questions.explanation: To use the front brake, squeeze the lever firmly and smoothly with all four fingers. Apply more pressure gradually.

questions.question: If the throttle gets stuck, you should:

options.text: Jump off the motorcycle.
Apply the brakes.
Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Do not try to twist the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: If your throttle gets stuck, try twisting it back and forth several times. If this does not free it, immediately use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of the lane should you use?

options.text: The left part of the lane
The center of the lane
The right part of the lane
Either the left or right part of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left part of the lane
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, ride in the left part of your lane. This keeps you farthest away from car doors opening, people stepping out, and cars pulling out of spaces.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, tell them to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has started.
Sit as far forward as they can without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Talk whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk whenever they want.
questions.explanation: To keep you focused on riding, passengers should avoid talking and moving too much. Passengers should get on the motorcycle only after the engine has started. They should sit as far forward as they can without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Where does debris and oil from cars collect in a traffic lane?

options.text: In the center of the lane
On the sides of the lane where motorcycles should ride
Where most accidents occur
Where drivers are least likely to see a motorcyclist

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane
questions.explanation: Debris and oil from cars collect in the center of the lane. Utility hole covers and other hazards are also found there.

questions.question: What should you do if your front wheel begins to skid?

options.text: Keep the front brake engaged and ride it out
Keep the front brake engaged and release the rear brake
Release the front brake right away, then apply it again smoothly
Release the front brake and press harder on the rear brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again smoothly
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake immediately and completely. Then apply it again smoothly.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
Body weight
How fast the alcohol was consumed
How often a person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often a person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and body weight. A person's sex, physical condition, and food intake may also have some effect.

questions.question: Is hearing protection necessary for motorcycle riders?

options.text: No, not if you wear a helmet
Yes, you need it even with a helmet
Only on windy days
No, not if you carry a passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, you need it even with a helmet
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Hearing protection blocks harmful noise while still letting you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: What should you do if you must stop quickly while in a curve?

options.text: Straighten the motorcycle, square the handlebars, then stop
Apply both brakes hard while leaning
Use only the rear brake
Use only the front brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten the motorcycle, square the handlebars, then stop
questions.explanation: If you must stop quickly in a curve, straighten and square the handlebars first, then stop. If you cannot straighten, apply the brakes smoothly and gradually. Reduce your lean angle, then increase braking pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: Is the oily strip in the center of a lane safe for motorcyclists?

options.text: Never
Usually yes, but not when the road is wet
Usually yes, but not when it is sunny
Always, no matter the weather

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually yes, but not when the road is wet
questions.explanation: Oil drips from cars collect in a strip in the center of the lane. Unless the road is wet, this area usually provides enough grip for safe riding. The strip is usually no more than two feet wide, so you can often ride around it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: How should you swerve to avoid a hazard?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly
Turn the handlebars quickly
Press the handle grip in the direction you want to go
Press the handle grip in the opposite direction of where you want to go

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to go
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then press the right to recover. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: What should you do when braking on a slippery surface?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes
Press hard on the front brake to prevent the tire from locking
Use only the rear brake
Use one brake only

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the brake lever gradually to avoid locking the front wheel. Use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: What is a limitation of motorcycle windshields?

options.text: They are a good substitute for a face shield
They are a good substitute for goggles
They do not protect your eyes from the wind
They do not protect you from items thrown from other vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: They do not protect your eyes from the wind
questions.explanation: A windshield is not an adequate substitute for a face shield or goggles. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from the wind.

questions.question: When you must both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other
Do both at the same time and brake harder
Do both at the same time and focus mainly on swerving
Do neither action

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other
questions.explanation: You need good traction to swerve safely, so you should not brake and swerve at the same time. Instead, do one action and then the other.

questions.question: If your front tire locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the brake engaged until you stop completely.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the brake lever until the tire grips the road again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brake lever until the tire grips the road again.
questions.explanation: When your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake lever until the tire grips the road again. Then apply the brake again.

questions.question: Riders wearing helmets are ________ more likely to survive a crash than those without helmets.

options.text: Two times
Three times
Eight times
Ten times

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a head injury in a crash compared to not wearing a helmet.

questions.question: When in traffic, how much stopping distance do motorcycles need?

options.text: Much less distance than cars.
Less distance than cars.
The same distance as cars.
More distance than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same distance as cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the same stopping distance as cars when riding in traffic.

questions.question: When you are stopped, what gear should you be in?

options.text: First gear.
Neutral.
Fifth gear.
Any gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: First gear.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow down or stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular in shape?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Signs that show road rules, like speed limits, are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. Riders must follow the rules shown on these signs.
